| [ADR-001](ADR-001-adopt-the-revoy-decision-log-discipline-for-mcl.md) | Adopt the revoy decision-log discipline for MCL | Proposed | Design-only | MCL records its architectural decisions as standardized-frontmatter ADRs in decisions/, managed by revoy adr (new | list | index), so decision-debt is machine-visible to revoy slippage instead of living in chat transcripts and audit files. |
| [ADR-002](ADR-002-mcl-is-a-signal-validation-layer-not-an-agent-framework-or-a.md) | MCL is a signal-validation layer, not an agent framework or a game engine | Proposed | Design-only | Ratify the Stage 3 mandate as the project identity: the registry/arbiter/signal core is the product — a domain-, provider-, and framework-agnostic validation layer installable under anything — and interactive fiction is a demo domain, not the market. Do not compete on less-abstraction-than-a-raw-SDK; compete on deterministic replay, knowledge-boundary scoping, and content-addressed provenance. |
| [ADR-003](ADR-003-one-grammar-one-source-of-truth-bless-mcl-lang-as-the-canoni.md) | One grammar, one source of truth: bless mcl-lang as the canonical parser | Proposed | Design-only | mcl-lang is the canonical .mcl parser/validator/emitter; mcl-parse is frozen as a legacy shim until its callers (mcl-cli, mcl-wasm) migrate, then deleted. A spec-parity conformance test fails the build when docs/language-reference.md and mcl-spec/document.rs diverge (R2 drift class). |
| [ADR-004](ADR-004-carve-out-mcl-kernel-a-zero-i-o-zero-async-zero-ml-dependenc.md) | Carve out mcl-kernel: a zero-I/O, zero-async, zero-ML dependency firewall around the pure core | Proposed | Design-only | The pure deterministic core (spec, lang, signal, registry arbiter+log, policy) moves behind a dependency firewall as mcl-kernel; graph/memory/llm/server become clients of it. mcl-validate is the standalone CLI/product surface built on the kernel (subsumes roadmap M12.1). Gate: a cargo tree assertion that the kernel pulls no tokio/reqwest/fastembed/usearch. |
| [ADR-005](ADR-005-generation-time-constraint-is-first-class-compile-the-declar.md) | Generation-time constraint is first-class: compile the declared world to a decoding grammar | Proposed | Design-only | The world file compiles to a decoding constraint — GBNF/XGrammar-class grammars for open models, structured-outputs/forced tool-use for closed APIs — so an undeclared signal is unsamplable rather than merely detected. This supersedes the Stage-1 posture that structured output is a Plan-B fallback; the arbiter chain is demoted to safety net and drift detector. |
| [ADR-006](ADR-006-generalize-actionresolver-to-a-schema-shaped-toolresolver-tr.md) | Generalize ActionResolver to a schema-shaped ToolResolver trait | Proposed | Design-only | Replace the RPG-shaped ActionResolver with a ToolResolver trait that maps 1:1 onto JSON-schema tool/function definitions (name, typed args, return contract), so an MCP tool list or an OpenAI/Anthropic tool schema loads directly; combat/inventory become just two implementations (roadmap M12.2). |
| [ADR-007](ADR-007-bindings-strategy-mcl-py-pyo3-maturin-is-the-flagship-embedd.md) | Bindings strategy: mcl-py (PyO3/maturin) is the flagship embedding; one conformance corpus for every runtime | Proposed | Design-only | Productize the proven revoymcl binding as mcl-py (pip install mcl, maturin-built), promote the PyO3 path to primary with pure-Python as offline fallback and differential oracle (roadmap M12.3); ship mcl-wasm as an npm package second; one corpus of worlds+transcripts+expected-verdicts must pass identically on every binding. |
| [ADR-008](ADR-008-reliability-is-a-measured-recurring-property-the-battery-2-0.md) | Reliability is a measured, recurring property: the battery 2.0 doctrine | Proposed | Design-only | No reliability claim without a re-runnable battery: extend the April 2026 crypt sweep with 3+ non-RPG action vocabularies (filesystem, REST, approval), an adversarial suite measuring catch-rate against undeclared/hallucinated actions, and a recurring re-run cadence publishing a diffable, dated leaderboard (roadmap M14 + M16.2). The 2026-04-22 sweep is a pilot, not proof. |
| [ADR-009](ADR-009-honor-the-effect-system-memoize-pure-content-address-cacheab.md) | Honor the effect system: memoize Pure, content-address Cacheable, quarantine ReplayUnsafe | Proposed | Design-only | The runtime consults Effect per action: Pure results are memoized, Cacheable external calls are content-addressed and never re-paid, ReplayUnsafe is quarantined, IdempotencyKey dedups; the signal log gains rewind/fork-at-turn/diff-two-runs. Staged after the kernel carve-out (Stage 4). |
| [ADR-010](ADR-010-the-signal-log-becomes-a-verifiable-ledger-merkle-chain-port.md) | The signal log becomes a verifiable ledger: Merkle chain, portable export, independent verifier | Proposed | Design-only | Merkle-chain the accepted-signal log with optional signing; mcl audit export produces a portable transcript verifiable by a third-party CLI against the world+policies with no access to the original runtime. Governance-grade audit is the moat the comparison doc says nobody else has (Stage 4). |
| [ADR-011](ADR-011-mcl-verify-bounded-model-checking-over-declared-worlds-and-c.md) | mcl verify: bounded model checking over declared worlds, and certified worlds | Proposed | Design-only | Grow mcl-policy into a checker that answers reachability/invariant questions statically (no PHI export to non-auditors on any path, budget stays non-negative, no deadlock); mcl verify returns a proof or a counterexample trace; a certified world is a signed artifact attesting no-undeclared-action + no-policy-violation on any path (Stage 4, after the kernel). |
| [ADR-012](ADR-012-worlds-compose-policy-overlays-and-a-federated-arbiter.md) | Worlds compose: policy overlays and a federated arbiter | Proposed | Design-only | Formalize extends + policy-overlay composition so a signal must pass every overlay's policies; build toward a registry of vetted, versioned governance overlays (HIPAA, PCI, spend-confirmation) that are imported and composed like crates. The endgame stage — deliberately sequenced last (Stage 5). |
